claims.text: Before upgrading, record the current deployment and configuration, define explicit rollback triggers including performance problems and errors, and document the restore procedure, communication path, post-rollback monitoring, and failure review; validate the recovery process in staging. (medium confidence)

For self-managed Community deployments, plan a 7.0-to-8.0 rollback as restoring a backup taken before the upgrade rather than relying on a binary downgrade; rehearse and time the restore before production. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Set read-path rollback triggers against representative workload baselines instead of assuming every 8.0 read workload improves: MongoDB says performance gains vary by workload and configuration, and Percona's comparison of Percona Server for MongoDB 8.0.4 with 7.0.15 found individual tests where 7.0 was more than 5% faster. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-02-04)

As verified on 2026-10-23, MongoDB's 8.0 documentation says binary downgrades are unsupported for Community Edition, Enterprise binary downgrade requires support assistance, and only single-version downgrades are supported. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

After installing MongoDB 8.0 binaries on a 7.0 deployment, keep FCV at 7.0 through a burn-in and raise it to 8.0 only after tests make downgrade unlikely; FCV 8.0 enables persisted features that are incompatible with 7.0 and can complicate downgrade. (high confidence)

Atlas Core has a separate rollback path: an in-place major-version downgrade requires FCV to have been pinned before the upgrade; without that pin, MongoDB documents point-in-time or snapshot restore to a new cluster running the previous major version. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)
